intro:
Use it for a launcher that is opened from a hotkey: search the pages of an app, its settings and its actions in one place, and run one with Enter. For a field that answers a question in rows under it, use [Command Dock](/docs/web/components/command-dock). For actions on one thing, opened from a button beside it, use a [Menu](/docs/web/components/menu).

Items are written as children. Each hides itself when it does not match what is typed: every word has to appear in its title, its `subtitle`, its `kind` or its `keywords`, in any order. A group with nothing left in it hides too, and `Command.Empty` shows when nothing is left at all. The first match is highlighted, so a few letters and Enter run it.

The default layout, `spotlight`, is the large launcher: a tall field with a mark at its start, slim rows with the kind of each at their end, and a floating footer the last rows fade out under.

Put it in a `Command.Dialog` to open it over the page with ⌘K, or Ctrl+K, or leave it in the page. Opened from its hotkey it appears at once, with no animation, because a launcher is opened many times a day.
usage:
<Command.Dialog hotkey="mod+k">
  <Command>
    <Command.Input placeholder="Search for pages and actions…" />
    <Command.List>
      <Command.Group heading="Pages">
        <Command.Item icon={<BookIcon />} kind="Guide" onSelect={() => go('/docs')}>
          Documentation
        </Command.Item>
      </Command.Group>
      <Command.Empty />
    </Command.List>
    <Command.Footer>
      <Command.FooterAction keys={['↵']}>Open</Command.FooterAction>
    </Command.Footer>
  </Command>
</Command.Dialog>

parts.Dialog: Opens the launcher in a panel over the page, from its `hotkey` (`mod+k` by default, `null` for none) or from a `trigger`. Choosing an item closes it, unless the item has `closeOnSelect={false}`. Escape closes it too.
parts.Input: The field. It has focus while the launcher is open, and the arrow keys and Enter work from it. `icon` replaces the magnifying glass and `prefix` puts a chip before the text, such as the page a nested list is on. Its children go at its end.
parts.InputAction: A button at the end of the field, with its `keys` after its label, such as switching the field to asking an assistant.
parts.List: The results, scrolling inside the launcher. In the `split` layout the preview of the highlighted item sits beside it.
parts.Group: Items under a `heading`. It hides when none of its items match.
parts.Item: One result: `icon`, the title as its children, a quieter `subtitle`, and at its end a `badge`, its `kind` and its `shortcut`. `onSelect` runs when it is pressed or Enter is pressed on it. `keywords` are more words to find it by, and `forceMount` keeps it whatever is typed.
parts.Empty: Shown when no item is left.
parts.Loading: A spinner and a line, for results still on their way.
parts.Footer: The foot of the launcher: `lead` at its start, such as a `Command.FooterButton`, and its actions at its end. In `spotlight` it floats over the list as a round button and a pill of actions, and the last rows fade out under it; in the other layouts it is a bar.
parts.FooterAction: An action in the footer, with its `keys` after its label. The first is usually what Enter does.
parts.FooterButton: An icon button for the footer's start, such as one that opens a menu of settings. It needs an `aria-label`. Round in `spotlight`.
parts.FooterDivider: A thin rule between two footer actions.
parts.Keys: Keys drawn as key caps, for anywhere else in the launcher.

examples.title: In a dialog
examples.description: `Command.Dialog` with a `trigger` for a pointer and `hotkey` for the keyboard. Choosing an item runs its `onSelect` and closes the dialog. Opened from the keyboard it appears at once; opened with the button it fades in. This page's own search already has ⌘K, so the demo uses ⌥K.

examples.title: Compact
examples.description: `variant="compact"`: a dense palette for an editor, with smaller rows and each item's `shortcut` at its end.

examples.title: Grid
examples.description: `variant="grid"` lays the items out as tiles, `columns` to a row, and the arrow keys move across and down. The rows are cut from the items that match, so a filtered grid closes up rather than leaving gaps.

examples.title: Split
examples.description: `variant="split"` shows the highlighted item's `preview` beside the list, and moving with the arrow keys changes it. On a narrow screen the preview is left out.

examples.title: Inline
examples.description: `variant="inline"` sits in the page as a card, for a search page rather than a launcher. Anything can go between the field and the list; here a [Chip](/docs/web/components/chip) group narrows the results by section.

examples.title: Results from a server
examples.description: `filter={false}` stops the items hiding themselves, for results already filtered elsewhere. Hold the text with `search` and `onSearchChange`, and show `Command.Loading` while the request is out.

examples.title: Nested pages
examples.description: An item with `closeOnSelect={false}` can open a page of its own: swap the groups, show where you are with the field's `prefix`, and go back when Backspace is pressed in the empty field.

notes:
### Keyboard

The arrow keys move the highlight, Enter runs the highlighted item, and Escape closes a dialog. In the `grid` layout Left and Right move across a row. The hotkey opens and closes the dialog from anywhere on the page.

### Choosing a hotkey

A page never receives the keys a browser keeps for itself, such as ⌘T, ⌘W or ⌘1 to ⌘9. ⌘K and Ctrl+K are free to use and are what most launchers use. With more than one `Command.Dialog` on a page, or a search of your own already on ⌘K, give only one of them the hotkey and pass `hotkey={null}` to the rest.

### Accessibility

The field is a combobox and the results are a listbox, so a screen reader announces the highlighted item as the arrow keys move. The dialog is named by its `label`, `Command menu` by default. Shortcuts drawn by `shortcut` and `Command.Keys` are only shown; handle the keys where the action lives.
